verdict: CLOSING — a brand-new faceless channel can still technically get distribution (Lume cold-started Aug 2025 and hit 262k subs/41M views in 11 months), but every verified organic solo entrant in the EXACT adjudicated-fraud-documentary format since mid-2024 is dead-on-arrival (5–4,800 lifetime views), the one breakout is broader heist/crime content with suspected studio backing whose pure financial-fraud episodes are its worst performers, and a late-2025 AI-tutorial wave has flooded the entry point.

evidence_summary: METHOD: search.list was quota-blocked, and the sandbox egress proxy additionally blocked direct fetches of youtube.com, reddit.com, feedspot.com, similarchannels.com and lume-studio.ai (403 policy denials — not routed around). Discovery therefore ran on (a) WebSearch surfacing youtube.com/watch URLs, then videos.list → channelId → channels.list to verify every number via the API; (b) uploads-playlist scans (playlistItems.list) for per-video performance; (c) systematic probing of niche-obvious handles via channels.list forHandle (FraudDocs, MoneyScandals, CorporateCrimeFiles, FinCrime, FraudChronicles, GreedChronicles, CrimeAndCapital, WhiteCollarCrime...), which is how most failures were found. All subscriber/view/date figures are API-verified as of 2026-07-13. KEY FINDINGS: (1) The only verified sub-2-year faceless success touching adjudicated fraud is Lume — content began 2025-08-05, now 262k subs / 41.4M views / 108 videos — but its first-month videos opened at 270k+ views (consistent with studio backing/cross-promotion rather than a solo organic cold start), and its adjudicated-FINANCE-fraud episodes (Wirecard COO: 8,453 views) are its worst performers, 10x below channel median. (2) Every verified organic entrant in the EXACT court-records fraud-doc format since Mar 2024 failed: Financial Crime Stories (4 subs), Corporate Crime Files (2 subs), Fincrime (1 sub), Money Scandals (6 subs), FraudChronicles (5 lifetime views), plus three never-uploaded niche-named shells registered Dec 2024–Jan 2026 — all stalled within 1–8 weeks. (3) A late-2025 tutorial wave ('Build a Faceless Finance Documentary Channel with 100% free AI tools' — Digital Dollars, 144k views Nov 2025; AI Maskman, 30k views Dec 2025) is actively recruiting entrants into this exact format, which both explains the failure cohort and predicts continued crowding through Aug 2026. (4) Incumbents remain healthy: WSM's fraud uploads run 67k–200k views (Apr–Jun 2026); FINAiUS (AI-assisted, 776k subs) pulls 370k–1.1M per 45-min bank-fraud doc; ENDEVR's re-released crypto-scam doc took 74.6k views in 5 days (Jul 2026) — demand exists, but it is being captured by established libraries. SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS DISCLOSURE: my discovery method can only see failures that chose guessable handle names; web search structurally surfaces winners. The true denominator of failed 2025–26 entrants is certainly far larger than the 8 verified here (the tutorial videos alone have ~175k views), and there may exist mid-sized quiet successes invisible to both web search and handle-probing. Absence of any discoverable H1-2026 organic breakout after ~15 targeted searches is itself weak-to-moderate evidence none exists at scale.

answers.question: (1) CRITICAL: Is there any verified sub-2-year faceless channel succeeding on adjudicated-fraud case files?
answers.answer: Qualified yes — exactly one, with material caveats. Lume (UCRMHn-rak9qpukKv4-r8G5w): first upload 2025-08-05, today 262k subs / 41.37M views / 108 videos, faceless weekly 'original documentaries' including adjudicated financial-fraud cases (Jho Low/1MDB doc: 614,577 views; Wirecard/Marsalek; counterfeiting; crypto scams). Caveats that cut against the finalist's thesis: (a) the channel shell was created 2024-06-15, 14 months before content, and its videos opened at 271k–356k views in week one — a pattern consistent with a professional/AI studio operation (a 'Lume Studio, AI-native faceless channels, 1B+ views across 100+ channels' website surfaced in search but the site was unreachable to confirm the link), not a bootstrap; (b) within Lume's own catalog, the court-records financial-fraud episodes are the WORST performers (Wirecard COO 8,453 views vs ~100k channel median; '126,000 victims / 61,000 BTC' scam 14,170) while heists/hackers/cartels drive the channel. No verified solo, organic, sub-2-year channel succeeding on the exact adjudicated-fraud-case-file format was found; the five verified exact-format entrants (Mar 2024–May 2026) all have under 5k lifetime views. FD Finance (created 2023-12-18, 201k subs, 25.3M views) is the nearest miss at 31 months old and proves the format could still work for a 2024 entrant.

answers.question: (2) Do closed-case retrospectives hold demand 1–3 years after headlines — what does the view tail look like on older fraud documentaries across channels?
answers.answer: Yes — the catalog tail is real, with one honest caveat: the API exposes only cumulative views, not view velocity, so 'held demand' is inferred from old videos sitting far above their channel's typical per-video level (which requires continued post-publication accrual). Evidence across channels: Wall Street Millennial's 2023 closed-case docs now sit at 4–6x its current per-video median of ~87–93k (SBF sentencing doc, Oct 2023: 550,987; Celsius fraud, Oct 2023: 403,758; China P2P Ponzi, Jul 2023: 355,576; Evergrande $78B fraud, Apr 2024: 324,859; FatBurger fraud, May 2024: 597,623). Cases stay monetizable YEARS after adjudication: FD Finance's QuadrigaCX doc published Mar 2025 about a 2019-closed case took 240,044 views (1.2x its sub count); SLICE Full Doc's Allen Stanford doc (Jun 2024, case adjudicated 2012) 746,458; Best Documentary's Jordan Belfort upload (2021, 1999 case) 781,821; James Jani's SBF doc (Sep 2023) 10.18M; ENDEVR's re-packaged OneCoin doc took 74,579 views in its first 5 days (Jul 2026). Counter-signal: the tail accrues overwhelmingly to channels with existing authority/subscriber bases — the same closed cases published by cohort failures got 5–1,501 views, so the tail is a library asset, not an entry wedge.

answers.question: (3) Does AI-narrated true-crime-finance retain viewers — AI/faceless fraud channels vs voiced incumbents?
answers.answer: No public retention data exists (audience-retention curves are creator-private); proxies point to a two-tier outcome. Tier 1 — AI-assisted with strong editorial: FINAiUS (776k subs, 65M views, led by fintech entrepreneur Rocky Xu, openly promotes AI avatar/production tools) sustains 370k–1.12M views on 43–49-minute bank-fraud documentaries (Bank of America 1.12M, UBS 916k, State Street 371k, Wells Fargo 377k) — long-form AI-assisted finance-crime demonstrably holds audiences at scale, and Lume (likely AI-native production) averages ~383k views/video across 108 uploads. Tier 2 — commodity AI pipelines: the entire verified copycat cohort spawned around the late-2025 free-AI-tools tutorials is under 5,000 lifetime channel views each; none got algorithmic distribution at all, so retention never even became the binding constraint. Policy risk is non-trivial: YouTube terminated True Crime Case Files (millions of views) in Feb 2025 for AI-fabricated 'true crime,' and demonetized several sister channels — court-records-grounded content mitigates but does not eliminate this exposure. Versus voiced incumbents: Coffeezilla (4.7M subs), MagnatesMedia (1.85M), James Jani (2.21M) still own the niche's top end; no AI-narrated entrant matches their per-video engagement, and WSM's human-voiced 87–93k median exceeds what any post-2024 organic AI entrant achieves by 2–4 orders of magnitude.
